clips.take: The first of three identical takes; its opening burst, without the two-second low tail.
clips.why: A cartoon laser beam for the Martian ray. Named for it; the burst has its energy at 0.8 to 1.5 kHz in the first 200 ms.

clips.take: The flare shot (the first event, 0 to 0.64 s), without the burst that follows at 0.84 s.
clips.why: A flare leaving its tube for the Rocket Cart's firework: a noisy launch of a quarter of a second.

clips.take: The shot itself (it starts at 0.19 s), without the mechanism clicks before it and the long tail.
clips.why: A steampunk gun for the Clockwork Gunner. It is one shot, not a burst.

clips.take: The shot and the first 0.8 s of its 3.8 s tail.
clips.why: A steampunk cannon for the Steam Cannon: the name and the unit match.

clips.take: The first of four punches in a row (they come 0.3 s apart): a thump at 0.12 s and its burst of noise.
clips.why: A cartoon punch for a hit that lands.

clips.take: The impact (0.05 to 0.25 s and its ring), without the click that comes 50 ms before it.
clips.why: A heavy mechanical impact for a siege shot or a charge that lands: a tight thud around 100 Hz with a knock at 2 kHz.

clips.take: The blast and the first second of its tail (the file is one explosion of 1.9 s).
clips.why: A medium explosion for a bomb or a rocket that bursts.

clips.take: The first half second: the break and the shards up to the second burst at 0.44 s.
clips.why: Glass breaking and falling stands in for ice that cracks: bright, between 3 and 9 kHz.

clips.take: The third of four takes (6.15 to 6.83 s), the shortest: a tone that climbs from 0.75 to 5.9 kHz in half a second.
clips.why: A short power-up for a unit that is promoted or grows.

clips.take: 0.85 s from the start of a 5.3 s rumble of falling rock, with its own fades.
clips.why: Earth and rock moving for a Mole that tunnels.

clips.take: The first 0.38 s of a 5.7 s pneumatic hiss, faded out.
clips.why: A pneumatic hiss for a puff of steam. It is bright: its energy is around 8.7 kHz.

clips.take: The first of four identical takes: its first four swings (a tone going up and down between 0.4 and 1.1 kHz, each swing quieter).
clips.why: A cartoon spring for a Candy unit that bounces.

clips.take: The blow and its ring (the first 0.2 s), without the chips that fall after it.
clips.why: A hammer on stone for something being built. It rings at 5.4 kHz.

clips.take: The whole click: two ticks 30 ms apart, the second quieter.
clips.why: An interface click for a button.

clips.take: The whole throw of the switch: two light clicks, then the clack at 0.12 s.
clips.why: A small lever switch for a setting switched on or off.
